title: Choosing Perplexity Alternatives by Limits in 2026
summary: Perplexity alternatives include tools like Activepieces with 741 integrations. Compare pricing, usage limits, and features to choose the right one.
body_markdown:
## 6. Kagi Search for ad-free searching


### Kagi plans and search caps


There is no free tier worth building a workflow on, so Kagi suits people who search all day and will pay to stop seeing ads.


The tier you leave Perplexity's free plan for is a paid one from the first query, and the price rises as the search caps come off.


"I hit my limit mid-afternoon" is the user-reported symptom in this category. On[Kagi's pricing page](https://kagi.com/pricing) , the Starter plan costs $5 a month and includes 300 searches.


viz type=stackrank title="What each Kagi plan costs per month" unit="$ per month" source="Kagi -[https://kagi.com/pricing"0](https://kagi.com/pricing) costs less than half of Ultimate at $25, with Starter at $5." Starter: 5 Professional: 10 Ultimate: 25


That's roughly ten a day, so a heavy searcher will run out before the month does. It's a trial-sized allowance, not a daily-driver one.


**Professional costs $10 a month with unlimited searches** . That's the point where the cap stops being the reason you leave.


Ultimate costs $25 a month, also unlimited, so the extra $15 over Professional buys no additional search volume. If you want that tier, confirm in the pricing page's feature list what it adds before paying, because the search count isn't the difference.


The takeaway is that the jump from Starter to Professional removes the cap for $5 more, while the jump to Ultimate removes nothing further on that measure, so you won't gain additional searches by upgrading to Ultimate.


### What Kagi replaces from Perplexity


Kagi gives you the integrations that Perplexity's free tier doesn't: no ads, AI answers alongside ranked results, and control over which sites rank higher or lower.


You can push a source you trust up and a content farm down.


For comparison,[Perplexity's Pro plan](https://www.perplexity.ai/pro) is $17 a month when billed annually, which means you must commit to paying for a year upfront.


Professional Kagi at $10 costs less than that, but it buys a different thing: a search engine with AI features, not an answer engine with search behind it.


Because Kagi is search-first, it won't replace a general assistant you already pay for. If your limit was the number of answers or the model quality, Kagi doesn't touch it.


If your limit was ads, tracking or a lack of control over sources, it addresses exactly that, and the money buys you out of it.
